jobs.description: Wir suchen ab sofort unbefristet eineLehrkraft für Englischin TeilzeitDer derzeitige Einsatzort ist das Learning Centre in der Haidebachstraße 1 in 63808 Haibach. Mit Helen Doron bietet unser Learning Centre Kurse für Babys, Kinder und Teens in Englisch und Spanisch an, die seit 40 Jahren weltweit auf Platz Nr. 1 stehen. In unserem Learning Centre unterrichten wir derzeit 150 Kinder aller Altersgruppen, von 3 Monate bis 19 Jahre. Die Einrichtung ist räumlich ansprechend und modern ausgestattet. Wir verstehen es als unsere Aufgabe, die Familien zu unterstützen, die ihre Kinder mehrsprachig erziehen möchten, und bieten diesen Kindern eine erweiterte Sprachheimat, in der sie Englisch oder/und Spanisch mit Freude, Spiel, Spaß und ganz ohne Leistungsdruck lernen. Mit neuen Methoden werden unsere Unterrichtsinhalte von speziell ausgebildeten Lehrern altersgerecht aufbereitet und umgesetzt. Und das mit großem Erfolg!Ihre Aufgaben bei uns:- Als Helen Doron Englischlehrer unterrichten Sie bei uns zunächst 2-5 Stunden pro Woche, je nach Ihrer Flexibilität und Erfahrung im Klassenzimmer. Celta, TEFL, PGCE, erstes/zweites Staatsexamen. Quereinsteiger sind aber auch herzlich willkommen. Wir bieten umfangreiche Schulungen und Unterstützung an.- Spaß daran haben, mit Kindern in einer aktiven, animierenden ausschließlich englischsprachigen Umgebung zu arbeiten.- eine positive Einstellung zu Kindern und zum Lernen haben.- über organisatorische Fähigkeiten verfügen.- im Landkreis Aschaffenburg wohnen.- unter der Woche nachmittags und vor allem samstags arbeiten möchten.- flexibel, verantwortungsbewusst und in hohem Maße selbstständig arbeiten können.- fit im Umgang mit Computern (v.a. iMac, iPad), Lernapps und analogen und digitalen Unterrichtsmaterialen sind.Wir bieten Ihnen:- einen angenehmen und flexiblen Beruf.- ein interessantes und vielseitiges Arbeitsfeld.- eine Lehrerausbildung, die Sie mit dem internationalen Diplom als Helen Doron Englischlehrer qualifiziert. - umfassende Möglichkeiten zur Fort- und Weiterbildung.- moderne Lehrmethoden, die Ihnen helfen, Kindern einen besseren Start ins Leben zu ermöglichen und ihnen dabei viel Freude und Spaß zu bereiten. - ein sicheres Einkommen, abhängig von Ihrer Ausbildung und Erfahrung.Einkommen für Einsteiger (pro Stunde incl. jobs.description: Our goal: 1% of the global Greenhouse Gas (GHG) reduction with our electrolysers!Are you ready to make your contribution to the energy transition? As a technological pioneer, we at H-TEC SYSTEMS have played a key role in shaping hydrogen technology for 25 years. We develop and produce innovative PEM electrolysers and electrolysis stacks for green hydrogen production. We combine the agility of a start-up with the advantages of the global sales network and the large-scale project experience of MAN Energy Solutions as well as direct access to Volkswagen's competence and experience in the area of production scaling and in supplier-based series business. We are a fast-growing company that offers you unique creative freedom and individual development perspectives.Our core principle is the passion to grow. To grow H-TEC, to grow closer as a team and personally. This means, we act as equals. Transparent, responsive, and helpful - to shape a culture of collaboration where we keep learning and improving ourselves. Are you up for a new adventure?Your Tasks-You will work closely with colleagues in Process Engineering based in the USA-You are responsible for the adaption and optimization of innovative PEM electrolyzers for the US market-You will review and work on process engineering and explosion protection issues in plant engineering, with a focus on standardization and compliance with US standards-You are responsible for reviewing risk assessments-You create and maintain the technical documentation and, in particular, take care of process flow diagrams (P&ID), requirement specifications, data sheets and specifications using relevant standards-You not only act as the internal contact person for your counterpart in the USA but also work closely with suppliers and external service providers-You collaborate across teams within the companyYour Profile-You have a degree in process engineering (plant design); alternatively, in environmental engineering, chemical engineering or a comparable qualification, a previous apprenticeship is desirable-You have knowledge of US standards (e.g., ANSI, ASME, NEC etc.) in the field of oil, gas and plant construction and are experienced in working with explosion protection in plant construction-You have several years of experience in plant engineering for process plants or power plants-You are business-fluent in written and spoken English-You have sound knowledge of the design of process circuits and are confident in the application of relevant standards and guidelines-You are very familiar with technical documentation, especially P&IDs-You work independently, are responsible, have a quick grasp, and enjoy analytical and creative activitiesWhat makes us thriveHydrogen is now – Shaping the future of tomorrow with Your helpFlexible organization of working hours and locations is important to us. We live mobile working and trust you that you can design it for yourself in the best possible way within the framework of your job.At regular all-hands meetings, you are always up-to-date and actively feel our growth and the associated changesH-TEC continues to green – always be in contact with new colleagues at weekly coffee talks and thus always connect anewSaving 1% GHG is only possible together – pull together with strong team spirit and collegial cooperationOur onboarding process, you will be accompanied through your first months with us in our mentoring programFor the daily energy flow we provide drinks and vitamin C - in addition, if you are permanently employed in Germany, you have the opportunity  to contribute privately to our 1% goal with a JobBikeH-TEC is growing, we are growing as a team and we want you to grow personally– this is our company mission with the Growing Together Initiative. We are working to offer you the best development opportunities in a rapidly changing environmentAt H-TEC, we are looking for future-oriented contributors of the energy transition. At no time do we make decisions based on skin color, origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender, disability or age. Not only do we continue to grow, but we also continue to operate in a global context. So our company is greening in diversity and making us better and more individual. Work in a healthy and green company that fights discrimination and exclusion of any kind.Deine Aufgaben-Du arbeitest eng mit den in den USA stationierten Kollegen im Bereich Process Engineering zusammen-Du bist verantwortlich für die Entwicklung und Optimierung von innovativen PEM-Elektrolyseuren für den US-Markt-Du prüfst und bearbeitest Themen im Bereich Prozesstechnik und EX-Schutz im Anlagenbau, wobei dein Fokus auf Standardisierung und Konformität zu US-Normen liegt-Du bist verantwortlich für die Prüfung von Risikobeurteilungen-Du erstellst und pflegst die technische Dokumentation und kümmerst dich insbesondere um Prozessfließbildern (P&ID), Lastenhefte, Datenblätter sowie um Spezifikationen unter Anwendung relevanter Normen-Du agierst nicht nur als initaler Ansprechpartner für dein Pendant in den USA, sondern arbeitest auch eng mit Lieferanten und externen Dienstleistern zusammenDein Profil-Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Verfahrenstechnik (Anlagenplanung); alternativ der Umwelttechnik, Chemietechnik oder vergleichbare Qualifikation.-Du besitzt Kenntnis der US-Normen (z.B. jobs.description: Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in Plant Interaction EcologySenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01.02.2027 :Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in Plant Interaction Ecology(Full-Time / Part-Time ** ** options available)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: Full-Time; Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, limited to 3 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.The announced position is part of a newly established research group studying plant environment interactions. The successful candidate will contribute to shaping the group's research programme and develop an independent research project aligned with the group's broader interests.Your tasks- Conduct internationally recognized research on how plant-animal interactions shape plant regeneration- Advance a mechanistic understanding of how plant-animal interactions and regeneration processes influence plant responses to climate and land-use change, e.g., shifts in species ranges or ecological novelty- Design and conduct field experiments, e.g., testing drivers of plant establishment, intraspecific variability, or the role of animal-mediated seed dispersal in forest dynamics- Develop and apply ecological models that integrate experimental findings with long-term datasets, linking individual-level processes to population dynamics and species range shifts- Publish research findings in leading international, peer-reviewed journals- Develop competitive proposals for third-party research funding- Supervise and mentor BSc, MSc, and PhD students- Contribute to teaching at the Bachelor’s and Master’s levels- Contribute to the development of the Interaction Ecology and Climate research groupYour profile- A doctoral degree, completed or nearing completion, in ecology, botany, biology, or a closely related field- A strong background in ecology, with research experience in plant ecology and or interactions between plants and animals- Demonstrated experience in designing and conducting field experiments- Experience conducting fieldwork under challenging conditions, e.g., in alpine environments or remote forest areas- Strong quantitative skills, including experience with advanced statistical methods such as Bayesian hierarchical models and data integration (combining heterogeneous datasets) and/or demographic or process-based population models, preferably using R- A strong publication record relative to career stage- Motivation to develop independent research on plant regeneration and biotic interactions in the context of climate and land-use change- Ability to work independently and collaboratively, and a willingness to contribute to teaching and student supervision- Fluency in spoken and written EnglishDesirable skills- An interest in science communication and public outreach- Proficiency in German, particularly for contributing to teaching and outreach activitiesWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV with a full publication list, copies of certificates and diplomas, along with the names of two referees) as a single PDF by 13 December 2026.Apply online via:https://short.sg/j/68770090by pressing the "Apply now" ButtonApplications via email cannot be considered.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Eike Lena Neuschulz at:eike-lena.neuschulz@senckenberg.de****For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung.

jobs.description: ...you're in the middle of itThe position is embedded in EU-MIC (European Coalition for Mental Health Medicines Innovation) , a strategic initiative led by the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) . EU-MIC aims to address the growing innovation gap in psychopharmacology between Europe and the United States and to examine the structural disparities between mental and somatic health in access to innovative medicines.A major workstream of the project focuses on the quantification of the direct and indirect societal costs of mental disorders , including:- healthcare and treatment costs- sick leave, retirement and disability-related costs- productivity losses- presenteeism and absenteeism- broader social and long-term economic consequencesThe resulting evidence will contribute to scientific publications, European policy reports, and advocacy activities targeting regulators, HTA bodies, payers, policymakers, clinicians, patients, and carers.The position is initially limited to two years, with the possibility of extending it to three years.
